text: So... x86 or Arm? Which one actually runs your code faster?
We had Claude write fast C for thirteen little kernels, then ran every answer on a real AMD EPYC and an NVIDIA Arm box.
And honestly? It's basically a tie. Arm wins six out of thirteen.
x86 crushes the wide SIMD stuff, like matmul. Arm grabs CRC, prime counting, and transpose.
Fun one: Claude used Arm's built-in CRC instruction. Two point three times faster.
Memory? Pretty much the same. Arm just starts a hair lighter.
The catch? Only nine of thirty-nine x86 answers even compile on Arm.
It's all open. arch-kernels, on Prime Intellect's Hub.
